Filed live during the cup-lexicon rename (EI-8912 / WI-3618, 2026-07-10) while
renaming `rubrics/hive-coordination-health/` → `rubrics/pot-coordination-health/`.

## The race

A first-party rubric is bundled as a self-describing directory
(`rubrics/<id>/rubric.json` + `listing.json` + optional `METHOD.md`) but its LIVE
identity is a row in `harness_shared.harness_plans` (a rubric **is** a plan row —
see `packages/operator-core/lib/rubrics.ts`). The cold-start seeder
(`ensureFirstPartyRubricsSeeded`, wired into every `rubrics:list`/`get`/`search`
read) is **no-clobber per-id**: it scans the bundled dirs on disk and seeds any
`rubricId` that has **no** matching plan row yet, owner
`FIRST_PARTY_RUBRIC_SEED_OWNER` (`'first-party-bundle'`).

Renaming a rubric is therefore a two-sided move that must land atomically but
usually can't:

1. `git mv rubrics/<old-id>/ rubrics/<new-id>/` (+ the ~N producer-file string
   constants) — a plain tree commit, picked up by git-sync on its own schedule.
2. A DB migration that renames the **live** plan row `<old-id>` → `<new-id>`.

Those two land as separate events. The moment (1) is live on disk but (2) hasn't
run yet, **any** background operator process's lazy seed pass (a live dev/bg-host
process, another agent's session, a fresh boot) sees the new directory with no
plan row under the new id yet — and seeds a **blank** row for it
(`owner='first-party-bundle'`, today's date, no real ratification history). When
migration (2) then runs, you have TWO rows: the real historical one (still under
the old id, about to be renamed) and a spurious first-party placeholder already
squatting the new id.

This isn't a maybe — on any box with background workers running (which is every
shared dev box), the window between "file rename commit lands" and "DB migration
applies" is measured in minutes, and the seed pass fires on every rubric read.
Assume it WILL happen.

## The fix — every rubric-rename migration must do this

Before renaming the real row into the new id, unconditionally clear a
same-id **placeholder** (never a real row — gate on `owner='first-party-bundle'`
so you never clobber a genuinely-existing rubric that happens to already use
that id):

```sql
DO $$
BEGIN
  -- Clear a same-id placeholder the disk-scan seeder may have raced in ahead
  -- of us — never touch a real (non-seed-placeholder) row under the new id.
  DELETE FROM harness_shared.harness_plans
   WHERE plan_slug = '<new-id>'
     AND owner = 'first-party-bundle';

  -- sql-snippet-justified: a one-off seed-race REPAIR (guarded rename), not a read —
  -- no tool exposes an atomic exists/not-exists precondition on a plan row.
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM harness_shared.harness_plans WHERE plan_slug = '<old-id>')
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM harness_shared.harness_plans WHERE plan_slug = '<new-id>')
  THEN
    UPDATE harness_shared.harness_plans
       SET plan_slug = '<new-id>',
           template_data = jsonb_set(COALESCE(template_data, '{}'::jsonb), '{methodRef}', '"<new-id>"', true)
     WHERE plan_slug = '<old-id>';
  END IF;
END $$;
```

This is idempotent and safe regardless of which order the two processes land in:
if the seeder hasn't raced yet, the `DELETE` is a no-op; if it has, the migration
clears its placeholder before the real rename, so you never end up with two rows.

Worked example: `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/531-rename-hive-coordination-health-rubric-to-pot.sql`.

## Since WI-3617: an invalid seeder-owned row self-heals (but the migration rule stands)

On 2026-07-17 a DB-recovery pass left the live `pot-coordination-health` row with
`template_data = NULL` under `owner='first-party-bundle'` — invisible to every read
(`planRowToRubric` nulls invalid rows) yet, under the raw-slug no-clobber check,
permanently blocking its own re-seed. The seed decision core (`rubricsNeedingSeed`)
now RECLAIMS a row that is both seeder-owned AND schema-invalid: it counts as
needing seed and `proposeRubric` upserts the bundle content over it on the next
rubrics read. A half-authored row under any real owner still blocks, invalid or
not. This makes the wedge class self-healing, but a rename migration must STILL
clear the placeholder first — a raced placeholder is usually *valid* (the seeder
writes full bundle content), so the reclaim never fires for it, and its lack of
ratification lineage is the reason it must not become the renamed row's identity.
Repair worked example (placeholder clear + tenant-scoped rename + content re-sync):
`libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/621-repair-pot-coordination-health-rubric-row.sql`.

## Why this lives here and not as a TS helper

Migrations are plain, standalone `.sql` files applied by the migration runner —
there's no code path for them to call a shared TypeScript helper. The
recurrence guard is this doc (discoverable via `docs:search` /
`agent-insights-index`) plus the pointer left in `rubrics.ts` next to
`FIRST_PARTY_RUBRIC_SEED_OWNER`, so anyone reading the seed code — not just
anyone who happens to find the 531 migration first — learns about the race
before authoring the next rubric rename.

## Checklist for the next rubric rename

- [ ] Rename the on-disk dir + producer-file string constants in the same commit.
- [ ] In the SAME migration that renames the DB row, DELETE a same-id
      `owner='first-party-bundle'` placeholder first (copy the snippet above).
- [ ] Don't forget `template_data->>'methodRef'` if the rubric has one — it's a
      real stored field (unlike `rubricId`, which derives from `plan_slug`).
- [ ] Verify no FK dependents before renaming `plan_slug` (it's the PK); other
      tables reference it as a loose string and historical rows are meant to
      stay under the old id (an immutable log of what happened under that id).
